brief: A tee connector in PETG (FDM, printed on its side so the layers stack along Y) for a rack made of 20 mm OD tube. A top rail runs straight through it along X (centre line y = 0, z = 0); a leg tube goes down from it along -Z and bottoms out 2 mm below the rail. Both tubes slip in (drawn at 20 mm) and are held by the joint itself. The tee stays inside x = -35 to 35, y = -16 to 16, z = -45 to 16. The rail is what holds the tee. The leg carries 150 N up from the floor, and a racking push of 30 N on the leg's foot, 400 mm below the rail, either way along X or Y. Safety factor 2.5.
note: Twin of tube-tee-20mm-petg, written as check now advises: the rail bears on its bore (push radial) with friction 0.3 for PETG on aluminium, in place of a bore fixed all round. The cold case passed on that glue with a saddle under the rail that slides off once the rail can only push.
